hints: A knight's tour visits every square once, so use backtracking to choose each next legal unvisited jump.
Warnsdorff's heuristic tries next squares with the fewest onward options first, making dead ends appear early.
A complete path must contain n^2 squares; if search gets stuck, backtrack.
analogy: Leave the tightest square choices for early, because flexible squares can wait.
correctness: Backtracking explores candidate tours without repeating a square; when all squares are visited the path is a legal tour, while ordering changes only search speed.
complexity: Worst-case exponential search; O(n^2) memory for the board and path.
algorithm: The input gives the knight's starting square. Backtrack from it, marking each visited square with its step number; order legal unvisited knight moves by fewest onward options (Warnsdorff) and undo on a dead end. Print the 8x8 step-number grid.
example: Starting at the given square, label it 1. Every later label must be one legal knight move from the previous label and must use a previously unvisited square; the final board contains labels 1 through 64.
